chunks: ʿAlī ibn Mahziyār, from Abū ʿAlī ibn Rāshid, said:

I said to Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام: What do you say regarding furs? In which of them may one perform salat (prayer)? He said: “Which furs?” I said: al-fanak, al-sinjāb, and al-sammūr. He said: “So perform salat (prayer) in al-fanak and al-sinjāb; but as for al-sammūr, do not perform salat (prayer) in it.” I said: Then foxes—may one perform salat (prayer) in them? He said: “No, but they may be worn after the salat (prayer).” I said: May I perform salat (prayer) in the garment that is next to it? He said: “No.”

key_terms.الثَّعَالِبُ: foxes, meaning fox fur, which is not permitted in salat (prayer)
key_terms.الثَّوْبِ: the garment or clothing item in question
key_terms.السَّمُّورُ: sable fur whose use in salat (prayer) is forbidden here
key_terms.السِّنْجَابَ: squirrel fur whose use in salat (prayer) is permitted here
key_terms.الْفَنَكَ: a type of fur whose use in salat (prayer) is permitted here
key_terms.الْفِرَاءِ: furs or fur garments under discussion for salat (prayer)

ai.seo_question: Which animal furs may be worn during salat (prayer) according to Imam Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام?
ai.summary: This hadith gives a legal ruling on performing salat (prayer) in garments made from certain furs. Abū Jaʿfar عليه السلام permits salat (prayer) in al-fanak and al-sinjāb, forbids it in al-sammūr and fox fur, and also disallows praying in a garment that directly touches such fur.
